items.title: Hackers Abuse YouTube Gaming Channels and SEO Poisoning to Deploy RATs and Chrome Hijacker
items.description: Hackers are turning ordinary searches and gaming videos into malware traps. A long-running campaign used YouTube channels and search-engine manipulation to steer victims toward installers that looked like useful software, game tools or performance fixes. items.title: Hackers Abuse AutoIt to Inject AsyncRAT Into Microsoft-Signed Windows Process
items.description: Hackers are using a familiar Windows automation tool to hide AsyncRAT, a remote-access trojan, inside a trusted system process. The campaign starts with a deceptive batch file named “Right-click to open Invoice Details.bat,” which can appear harmless to someone expecting an invoice or shared document. items.title: NCSC Warns of Critical Check Point VPN Flaws as Large-Scale Exploitation Is Expected
